short_version: The revision resolved 35 of the 58 round-1 findings, left 20 partly resolved, and deferred the 3 issue-body edits to jhan; nothing regressed.

Four new major gaps remain: the 8-lane build guidance orders code and test runs for a configuration whose baseline tests do not compile, the NaN test rule ignores that TRON_IGNORE_NAN is on in every production build, the child section never switches the K storage member to the new owner, and the definition of done depends on reviewer answers that have no place to be recorded.
Verdict: accept with changes. After those four edits and an honest status column in section 9, another agent can implement the parent from this page.
verdict_sub: 3 of 3 judges; 4 major edits and the section 9 column come first; see section 8
changes_outro: The revised page cites round-1 findings by id in brackets, for example [F05], and links each id to this page's anchors. This round keeps an anchor for every round-1 id (section 3), so those links still resolve. The round-1 page itself is archived unchanged as [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html), with its votes on [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1-votes.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1-votes.html).

dispo_intro: Each of the 58 round-1 findings was checked against the revised text by one checker agent and then independently re-graded by two adversarial re-graders (a source-truth lens and a fairness lens). The status below is the majority of the three. No id had a split vote (three different statuses). Three ids were not unanimous (F12 and F38 majority partly, F43 majority resolved); I accepted the majority in each case and changed no status myself.

A finding graded partly is not a failure of the revision. In most of the 20 cases the headline recommendation is met and what is missing is a refinement the round-1 verifiers had recorded under the finding. Section 4 turns the residuals that matter into new findings (N.. ids) so they have evidence and a recommendation of their own; the table below names them.
dispo_outro: The three deferred ids (F19, F20, F21) concern the public issue body. Codex correctly left GitHub untouched, and jhan owns the issue text. The design should still carry the proposed text and name jhan as the owner (N42), so the deferral is acceptable but not finished.
questions_intro: Round 1 asked codex to list its departures from Ben's sketch as questions for him instead of asserting them. The revision has a four-row "Questions for the reviewer" table with a proposed answer per row, marked as proposals pending agreement. The table below checks whether the four questions cover every departure and whether an implementer can act on them.
questions_rows: Q1. May the address formula live in each concrete view? Proposed: yes, with separate V and K families and separate owners.
Folding the layout type into the view (Ben's reservation, jhan's reading) and the two-family consequence (no single vnni_tensor<Layout> template).
Right question and right proposed answer. The cost of two families (duplicated conversion and access plumbing) is stated in the answer, which is enough for Ben to weigh it.
Q2. Should a const view object prevent mutation of its elements? Proposed: yes, at both matrix and row rank.
The departure from Ben's std::span rule (round-1 F04).

Right question. The revision now says the repository precedent is mixed (design section 2) and chooses the matrix rule for both new types. It cites only the rank-2 source; the rank-1 comment that states Ben's rule is not linked (N46, note).
Q3. May the view provide operator[] as well as at(token, dimension)? Proposed: yes; at() stays as an equivalent bounds-checked spelling.
The departure from Ben's at()-only access (round-1 F02).

Right question. It should say why the expr base needs operator[] (it indexes rows through it) and why Ben's sketch had no operator[] (a two-argument accessor cannot be spelled with one subscript), so Ben sees the trade (N09, minor).
Q4. Is the smaller parent scope sufficient? Proposed: yes; slices, iteration and generic writes are deferred.
The scope cut round 1 asked for (F08) versus Ben's "usual tensor operations".
Right question. The deferred list in section 5 is concrete. The design should say which sections change if Ben answers no (N07, note).
Missing: who asked for native K in the parent, and does Ben agree?
Typing the native-K kernel parameter goes beyond Ben's sketch, which types only the packed planes. jhan asked for it (prompt item 4, issue #4525).

Design section 2 calls it "the requested parent scope" without naming the requester, in a table whose other rows are Ben's requests. Name jhan as the requester and either add a fifth question or say that jhan owns this decision (N08, minor). All three judges rated the questions block inadequate on this point.
questions_outro: One gap applies to every row: the design never says where an answer is recorded or what the implementer does if no answer exists when work starts, while the definition of done requires recorded answers (N04, major). The recommended fix names the record (a comment on issue #4525 posted by jhan, copied into the parent PR description under a Decisions heading) and the fallback (implement the proposed answers and mark each decision as proposed).
edits: **Section 2 and the definition of done (N04, N08).** Add: "Answers are recorded as a comment on issue #4525, posted by jhan, and copied into the parent PR description under a Decisions heading. If no answer exists when implementation starts, implement the Proposed answer column and mark each decision as proposed." Change the definition-of-done item to "Each reviewer question has an answer recorded in the parent PR description, marked accepted or proposed, and the implemented interface matches it." At the native-K bullet, name jhan (issue #4525) as the requester and either add a fifth question for Ben or state that jhan owns the decision.

**8-lane build guidance (N01, M01, N61, N16, N12, N23, N24).** Replace the both-chunk-width sentence with: "The class definitions of v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row are complete in both builds (members are a bf16 array, a pointer and small integers). Their operation bodies (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, chunk, bf16_chunk) and every packed-V test case compile only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16. The typed kernel declarations and the fake definitions stay unconditional." Rewrite the 8-lane row: at unmodified main, t_llama_unit and t_heterogeneous_scheduler do not compile in this configuration, because page::set_v and page::get_v exist only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 [kv_cache.hpp:1616-1674]; the 8-lane check for the parent is configure, build the tron library and t_amx_dispatch_dtype, run t_amx_dispatch_dtype. Then decide the 8-lane set_v story once: either the parent adds an 8-lane page::set_v forwarder and removes the #if in save_v_impl, or it keeps v(...).set() and the #if; give the per-build width rules (16-lane set_v/get_v head_size % 32, scaled_v_expr {64,128,256,512}; 8-lane scaled_v_expr head_size % 64) and drop the 8-lane branch of page::v_tensor unless a caller is named.

**Child table (N03).** Add a row: "detail::kv_block K member: when k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> holds, the K member is k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size>, selected with std::conditional_t against the existing bf16s array as Ben's sketch shows. Keep sizeof(k) == sizeof(v), 64-byte alignment and trivial default construction so the parent's block-array construction covers it. The packed-plane accessor (name it) returns kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).k.as_view(), never a cast; the four reinterpret_casts of the array at the child head [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1692, 1706, 1730, 1742] go away with it."

**NaN paragraph and the Bits and conversions test row (N02, F41).** Add: "TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug configuration [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-295, a PUBLIC option of tron]. The native and deb presets and the required Nix test build are RelWithDebInfo, so in every configuration in section 8 both paths truncate identically (0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F80 on both). The 0x7F81 result appears only in the Debug presets asan, tsan and coverage." In the test row: guard generic-path NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN, or check the generic path only with finite, denormal and infinity inputs. Give the concrete bit example round 1 asked for (0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 versus 0x7F81) and drop the fp16 case, since _mm512_cvtph_ps quiets the NaN and neither path yields infinity for it.

**Section 9 (M05, N44, N43).** Add a column "Verifier corrections applied" (yes / partly / no) or split the 20 partly-addressed ids into rows labelled "Partly; remaining: ...". Replace "including its nine later corrections" with a sentence that says the nine C.. ids are the round-1 critic's additions. Say once what a bracketed id such as [F05] means and where the round-1 page is. Apply the F25 vocabulary fix the table already marks as accepted ("VNNI K layout", "shared block save", save = operation and store = instruction).

**Round-1 residuals that are one-sentence fixes.** F15/N29: "ten of the same files", and tell the agent to re-measure the conflict set with git merge-tree against the live tip (N30). F48/N37: the guard refuses when the CI lease is busy, when another person is active on the machine, or when a blackout window is set, and campaign_guard_acquire refuses while a runtron is running. F49/N41: make lint is the required check; make iwyu-check is an optional extra because the parent edits no public API header; name the platform key of the benchmark records (N38). F35/N13: omitting bf16_chunk silently selects the fp32 fallback, which is bit-exact but slower; a wrong signature is a compile error, not a silent fallback; detect the omission with a static_assert on the member type, not with a bit-pattern test. C02/N27: token_ix_needed is the page-readiness rule, not a partner rule. C06/N28: name the two Notes by their real titles and lines. C01/F12/N25: EAGLE exists only with uniform geometry, so the whole-arena array already covers its slot and the heterogeneous pass never meets it. F30/N45: say in the Short version that native K gets aliases and typed kernel parameters, not a new storage type. F38: add the V row unpack in full.hpp to the inspected call sites. F54: give the tile formula with its two block indices. F57: link the kernel signatures at f46e48ba. F58: state the rule files are byte-identical by blob id at the five commits. F08/N53: say the existing generic slice still accepts an lvalue packed view; only new slice code is deferred. C07/N57: say where k_vnni::index lives after the move. F29/N33: name save_k and save_k_helper and the two child test files the worker-index change touches.

**Callers and mechanisms the tables miss (M02, M03, M04, N15, N17).** Add book::fill_storage_slot / fill_random (test-only whole-block byte fill) to the callers table and to the search pattern; say it stays as is. Name the compile-check mechanism: requires-expression constants with STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE next to the existing ones in t_llama_unit.cpp:84-123, and rewrite page_supports_uniform_kv_access for the typed get_v destination. Name book::for_each_active_slot as the compile-time geometry loop for the heterogeneous construction pass, selecting slots by storage_location(...).reclaimable. State the aligned flag of the typed set_v source view at the model call site. Remove copy_plane or name its caller; the owner's defaulted copy already gives a byte copy.

**Interface details (N14, N20, N22, N51).** Say which header defines the native_k_view aliases and that the Stride default lives in view.hpp, so the interface header forward-declares the primary template without repeating the default. Extend the no-public-pointer rule to v_vnni_row's constructor. Admit that the K alias equals today's view type, so it rejects raw pointers but accepts any 64x128 bf16 view. Give dma its documented meaning (DMA-safe memory, contiguity tracked separately) or drop the reason clause.

**CI evidence (N36, N39).** Say what counts as execution evidence: the GCP Nix Test host job log of a run whose test steps ran (first attempt with a changed test runtime, or a GitHub rerun), showing Slice executing the named cases; a green check whose steps were skipped by a cached passage marker is not evidence. Note that the native preset probes the host and turns AVX512 off on a host without it, so -DAVX512=ON is not a guarantee.

**Words and page (N05, N06, N11, N48, N62).** Define "the reviewer" once (Ben, the tron maintainer) and separate the two Claude sessions by role. Define pair_base, kv_block_t, region_base, block_count and tile at first use. Say whose interpretation "The interpretation" is (jhan's). Name the live main tip at review time (2880c3aa9b) next to the recorded tip. Replace the 59 non-ASCII characters (title em dash, curly quotes, arrows, multiplication signs) with ASCII or numeric entities if the page is ever published as an artifact.

**Issue body (F19, F20, F21, N42, M06).** Keep the GitHub edits out of the design, but add a block "Proposed issue #4525 body additions (owner: jhan)" with the problem sentence, the three layout definitions, Ben's three straw-man constraints, and the roles-not-names wording, so jhan can paste it. Say how the parent PR body references the issue ("Refs #4525", not a closing keyword, because the child step follows).
verdict_intro: Three judges read the revised design with the dispositions and the confirmed new findings in hand, each from a different position: the implementing agent, the maintainer who wrote the straw-man, and a risk reviewer. All three returned the same verdict, accept with changes, and all three said the text is not yet implementable without a question to jhan or Ben beyond the four listed ones. All three also judged the questions block inadequate because native-K typing is not put to Ben.
verdict_outro: I agree with the judges. The 16-lane production path, which is the path that ships, is now specified correctly against live main: the save, load and copy chains, the partner-zero rule, the scaled_v bounds, the arena construction form and the lease rules all match the source. Nothing in the residual list would silently corrupt an attention sum. The four majors are about the 8-lane configuration, a test expectation, the child's K storage, and process; each is a one-paragraph edit.

Must change before implementation starts: edits 1 to 5 in section 7 (N04 and N08; N01 with M01 and N61; N03; N02; M05). Everything else can be fixed while implementing, and the implementer should treat the partly rows of section 3 as a checklist.
method: This round ran as one workflow of 268 agents (about 29.7 million tokens, 4,716 tool calls, 1 hour 51 minutes). Every agent read the same verified-facts files (round-1 facts and a round-2 addendum I verified myself against live main 2880c3aa9b before the run) and had read-only access to the tron worktree at the pinned commits, Ben's comments, jhan's prompts, the round-1 findings and the revised design text.

Disposition phase: 15 batches of related round-1 findings (2 to 4 ids each). One checker per batch graded each id and reported any new defect the fix introduced; two adversarial re-graders (source-truth, fairness) re-graded every id; the majority decided. 45 agents. Result: 35 resolved, 20 partly, 3 deferred, no split votes.

New-defect phase: 8 finders (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs) produced 81 candidates; the checkers added 17 more; a merge agent grouped the 98 into 62. Three verifiers per candidate tried to refute each one; 56 survived and 6 were rejected (section 9). A completeness critic added 8 candidates, and all 8 survived the same verification, for 64 new findings. Three judges then gave independent verdicts.

Limits. Nothing was compiled or run; the claim that the two test programs do not compile in the 8-lane build (M01, N61) is inferred from the #if guards in the source, not from a build. The design's pinned links were re-validated structurally (every local target exists; the 38 GitHub blob links are the same set as in round 1) but not fetched. This page was checked for pure ASCII, for an anchor per round-1 id, and for resolving local links; no browser render check was run on this host.
method_bullets: Data and scripts: evidence/claude-review-r2/ holds workflow-result.json (every agent's return value), findings.json (the data behind this page), build_findings.py and gen_review.py (the generator), overrides.json (my grades and prose), lead-verified-facts-r2.md (the facts I verified before the run), r1-findings-compact.md (the round-1 findings as the agents read them), design-revised-text.txt and design-revised-sha256.txt (the exact text reviewed).

Votes: every new finding's three votes and corrections are on [the round-2 votes page](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html); the disposition votes are inside the rows of section 3 (expand "Votes and evidence").

Round 1: the original review is archived as [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html) with its data in evidence/claude-review/. The revised design cites its ids; the anchors on this page keep those links working.

State at review time (2026-09-22 04:00 to 06:15 UTC): main 2880c3aa9b; PR 4424 draft on main at 30c4ac82cb, no reply after Ben's sketch; issue #4525 open, assigned to jhan, 0 comments, body unchanged since 00:11 UTC; issue #3997 open.

Severity re-grades by the lead after reading the votes: N12 to note (two of three verifiers: an omission of the 8-lane rule, not a wrong statement); N07 and N42 to note (the majority of their votes). The four majors kept their grade: N01 (two verifiers said minor on its own, but with M01 and N61 the 8-lane guidance as a whole would send the agent into a baseline compile failure), N02, N03, N04.

N01.lead_note: Two of the three verifiers graded this minor on its own: the class-completeness point was already in round-1 F11's verifier correction, and the design's sentence adopts F11's option A literally. I keep major because of what M01 and N61 add: the same 8-lane row tells the agent to run t_llama_unit and t_heterogeneous_scheduler in a configuration where, at unmodified main, neither compiles (page::set_v and page::get_v exist only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16). Taken together, the 8-lane guidance would send the implementer into a baseline failure and into writing AVX2 pair-extraction bodies that nothing calls. One rewrite of the both-chunk-width sentence and of the 8-lane row fixes all three findings.

N02.lead_note: I verified the macro myself: src/tron/CMakeLists.txt at 2880c3aa9b defines -DTRON_IGNORE_NAN for every non-Debug configuration as a PUBLIC option, and the native, deb and Nix test builds are RelWithDebInfo. So the design's sentence about the generic conversion setting a mantissa bit describes Debug builds only; in every build the design lists, both paths truncate identically. The consequence is a test-expectation trap, which is why this stays major although one verifier said minor: a NaN expectation written from the design's prose passes under asan and fails under the required Nix lane, or the reverse. The fp16 example round 1 gave was wrong for a second reason, which codex spotted: the hardware conversion quiets the NaN, so no fp16 NaN becomes infinity on either path.

N03.lead_note: I confirmed the gap in the child source: at 30c4ac82cb the K member of detail::kv_block is still the raw bf16s array, and k_vnni_plane, set_k_row, set_k_block and get_k_row all reinterpret_cast it (kv_cache.hpp:1692, 1706, 1730, 1742). The revised child table promises a k_vnni_view accessor but never says the member becomes the k_vnni_tensor owner, which is exactly the std::conditional_t selection in Ben's sketch and the construction rule the design itself states for V. One verifier graded minor because the design's other rules would block a cast route; I keep major because the child adaptation is the reason the parent exists, and this is its central sentence.

N04.lead_note: All three verifiers held this at major. The definition of done requires recorded answers; section 2 says the questions need no answer for the document; nothing says where an answer would be recorded or what the implementer does without one. The design does imply the PR 4424 thread as the place the questions get posted, so the precise defect is the missing record and fallback rule, not a missing venue.

M05.lead_note: The critic's point stands but the verifiers narrowed it: F54 is not an open residual, F48's guard sentences are true but incomplete rather than wrong, and F41 does name the macro. The honest fix is cheap: one column, or split rows for the 20 partly ids. It matters because a reader of section 9 alone concludes round 1 is closed, and the implementer would not know which residuals to check.

N13.lead_note: The verifiers agree on the mechanism: expr.hpp compares member-function pointers, so a wrong signature is a compile error and only a missing override falls back silently. They also agree the fallback is bit-exact for stored bf16 (the low 16 bits are zero after even_part or odd_part), so section 8's word lossy is wrong and a bit-pattern test cannot detect the omission. The revision introduced this sentence; the original design did not have it.

N17.lead_note: The revision followed the round-1 F13 recommendation literally, although two of the three round-1 verifiers had withdrawn the copy_plane suggestion in their corrections. That is a fair criticism of the round-1 page as much as of the revision: the recommendation text should have carried the correction. The fix is to drop copy_plane or name a caller.

N08.lead_note: The verifiers split on whether a fifth question is needed; all agree the requester is unnamed. Naming jhan and issue #4525 is the minimum. Whether Ben must agree to native-K typing is jhan's call, so the design may either ask Ben or say jhan owns it.

N41.lead_note: The four make targets exist. The defect is the word required applied to iwyu-check and the absence of make lint, which is the local form of the required Lint check. The run-tron-tests skill asks for iwyu-check only when a public API header changes, and the parent changes none.

N12.lead_note: Re-graded to note. Two verifiers showed the sentence is true in both builds (all four widths satisfy the 8-lane rule head_size % 64 == 0) and the defect is the missing 8-lane rule plus a misleading sentence order. Covered by edit 2.

rejected_r1_note.F09: Still rejected as a defect. The revision defers the generic-write scope for the round-1 F08 reason instead (design section 9).
rejected_r1_note.F36: Still rejected as a defect. The revision keeps the explicit rvalue overloads as a clarification (design section 9).
rejected_r1_note.F18: Still rejected. sw-dev-01 is codex's user-level build-host rule, not a repository rule; the design's sentence is codex following its instructions.
